items.title: Bank of Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high, flags concerns over inflation

ledger.what_new: BoJ raised rates to 31-year high; vote split 7-2 with two named dissenters
ledger.unique: Names dissenting board members Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato

clusters.state_of_play: The Fed raised rates a quarter point, its first hike since 2023; chair Kevin Warsh defended the Fed's independence. Trump initially lashed out, calling rates 'artificially high' and threatening trade halts with Mexico and Europe, but has since appeared to back Warsh, with stocks rallying; some GOP lawmakers expressed relief at Warsh's independence. The Bank of England held rates at 3.75% despite inflation hitting a five-month high (3.1%), warning borrowing costs may need to rise if energy-driven inflation persists. The Bank of Japan, facing pressure from the Fed's move and an unusual campaign by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, raised its rate by 0.25 percentage points to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995, in a 7-2 board vote with two dissenters, amid broader debt-cost and inflation concerns tied to the 10-year Treasury topping 5%.
